# Pack format

<!-- GENERATED by `fire docs` from server/*.go — do not edit by hand. -->

A pack is a folder `packs/<id>/` with `pack.json` (format `fire-pack-v1`) and, optionally, lesson files. The app reloads packs within a few seconds of a change. JSON Schema: [`pack.schema.json`](pack.schema.json). A complete small example: [`examples/packs/softmax`](../examples/packs/softmax/pack.json).

## PackFile

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | string | yes | Always `fire-pack-v1`. |
| `id` | string | yes | Pack id = folder name: lowercase latin letters, digits, dashes, up to 40 characters. Permanent: idea codes and progress depend on it. |
| `title` | string | yes | Title shown in the app. |
| `language` | string | no | Language of lessons, e.g. `ru` or `en`. |
| `description` | string | no | One or two sentences: what the learner will be able to do. |
| `topics` | []PackTopic | yes | Topics in teaching order. |

## PackTopic

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Topic slug, unique in the pack. The topic code is `<pack>.<topic>`. |
| `name` | string | yes | Topic title. |
| `definition` | string | no | One sentence about the topic. |
| `ideas` | []PackIdea | yes | Lessons (ideas) in teaching order: earlier ones are offered first. |

## PackIdea

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Idea slug, unique in its topic. The idea code is `<pack>.<topic>/<idea>` and never changes — progress is keyed by it. |
| `name` | string | yes | Lesson title. |
| `definition` | string | no | One sentence: the idea in plain words (used by search). |
| `level` | int | yes | 1 basic, 2 standard, 3 hard. A lesson is worth 3 + 3·level XP. |
| `lesson` | string | no | Lesson text in Markdown, 300–8000 characters. Math in KaTeX: `$…$` inline, `$$…$$` display. In JSON, backslashes are doubled: `\\frac`. |
| `lesson_file` | string | no | Instead of `lesson`: a Markdown file inside the pack folder, e.g. `lessons/negation.md` (single backslashes there). |
| `requires` | []PackLink | no | Ideas that must be learned before this one (they gate the lesson), with encompassing weights. |
| `uses` | []PackLink | no | Ideas this one exercises without needing them first: solving this lesson counts as partial review of them. Never gates. |
| `questions` | []Question | yes | 3–8 multiple-choice questions. Lessons ask them in order; reviews and quizzes draw from them. |

## PackLink

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes | Code of an existing idea in this or another loaded pack (`fire search` finds them). |
| `w` | float64 | yes | Encompassing weight 0.05–1: what share of a review of that idea a correct solve of this one counts as. See the rubric below. |
| `key` | bool | no | Requires only: the main prerequisite. If this lesson is failed, key prerequisites are scheduled for review at once. |

## Question

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question` | string | yes | The question, Markdown + KaTeX. |
| `options` | []string | yes | 3–6 distinct options. Put the correct one at different positions across questions. |
| `correct` | int | yes | 0-based index of the correct option. |
| `explanation` | string | no | Why the answer is right and the common mistake is wrong; shown after answering. |
| `difficulty` | int | no | 1–3, optional. |

## Weights: requires and uses

Each link says how much of the linked idea a correct solve of this lesson exercises. FIRe turns it into implicit review: the linked idea's stability moves the fraction w toward what an explicit Good review would give, and its recall gains w·(1 − R). Failing this lesson weakens ideas built on it and schedules its key prerequisites.

| w | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1.0 | Solving this lesson fully performs the linked idea, every time. |
| 0.7–0.9 | Uses it centrally in almost every question. |
| 0.4–0.6 | Uses a substantial part of it. |
| 0.1–0.3 | Touches it lightly. |

Rules of thumb: link the most direct ideas only, not their own prerequisites (credit flows down the graph by itself, multiplying weights along the path). Use `requires` only when the lesson cannot be followed without the idea; otherwise `uses`. Mark one requires link per idea as `key`. Requires links must not form a cycle. Implicit credit alone raises an idea's stability to at most 5× its last explicit review, and such an idea is still checked explicitly from time to time.

## What `fire validate` checks

- `pack.json` parses, has no unknown fields, `format` is right and `id` equals the folder name.
- Topic and idea ids are slugs and unique; names are not empty; `level` is 1–3.
- Each idea has exactly one of `lesson` / `lesson_file` (inside the folder), 300–8000 characters.
- 3–8 questions per idea; 3–6 distinct options; `correct` is a valid index; every question has an explanation.
- Math: `$` balanced; no control characters left by a single backslash in JSON (`\frac` must be `\\frac`).
- Every `requires` / `uses` code exists in a loaded pack (with a did-you-mean hint), weights are 0.05–1, no self-links.
- `requires` links across all packs form no cycle.
- Warnings: every correct answer at the same position; very long lessons.
